utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this has been a marathon, five days of testimony, but I know that you have it in you to do a sprint, nonetheless, to the finish, and I expect that we'll conclude this witness's examination-in-chief before the end of the first session. Since it's the first time that we're sitting in the afternoon, let me say that we'll sit to 3.45, then take a break of 20 minutes; then from 4.05 to 5.50, another break of 20 minutes; and then from 6.10 to 7.00 -- 7.15? Is it 7.00 or 7.15? I'm not certain. 7.00. I have been corrected. We have had six days of evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I shall be needing a geographical map for some questions that I'm going to ask General Stevanovic this afternoon, and the registrar was very -- has very kindly provided me with a map that they have at their disposal. It is a large map, so could somebody take it over, please, and put it on the easel or panel to the right of the witness or somewhere so the witness can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there an easel for it? Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, Mr. Robinson, yesterday or, rather, a moment ago - and I was told that the note came in yesterday from Mr. Nice - I was handed it a moment ago by Professor Rakic, and it says: "Prosecution provides the following information: [In English] September 1999, OTP investigator Dagsland was informed by the residents of the village of Kotlina, municipality of Kacanik, Kosovo, that 12 of the persons whose bodies were found in the wells in Kotlina following the attack on the village on 24th of March were KLA soldiers."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You received this from the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes. I have got it from Mr. Nice. It is signed "Geoffrey Nice, Principal Trial Attorney." Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, is that something the Trial Chamber should receive?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, it was provided to the accused under Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Rule 68. Provided to you pursuant to Rule 68, Mr. Milosevic. It may be helpful to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, do their names appear in the schedule of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think they do, yes. That's the whole purpose. The -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The book that I received published by the UCK or KLA with respect to their dead, this refers to a number of cases which are contained in Schedule B which relate to Bela Crkva, and of course the matter linked to Kotlina and a number of names. They don't all match. They don't all coincide, but it is easy to see what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, General, to draw the questions with regard to Kosovo to a close, in paragraph 63(k)(i) it is stated that our forces attacked the town of Kacanik on the 8th of March, 1999, or around that date -- I think, no. That is not Kacanik. It is (ii). On or about the 27th and 28th of March. So it is (k)(ii). Forces of the SFRY and Serbia attacked the town of Kacanik. Now, let me just ask you this, a very simple thing to begin with: At any time during that period or any time at all during the war, did the KLA forces hold any town in Kosovo and Metohija under their control?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, only for a very brief period of time they held the town of Orahovac in 1998. I think it was August or perhaps July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm asking you about the 27th and 28th of May, so that is the end of March 1999, was any town whatsoever under KLA control at that time?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, according to what it says in point (k)(ii), it would mean that the FRY forces attacked a town that they had under their control anyway, that our forces were attacking a town that was under their control. Would that emerge from what is stated here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be the conclusion from a formulation set out in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gentlemen, I would like to draw your attention to the fact when different villages are mentioned it is difficult to establish all the facts and data, but here the name of a town is mentioned. It says the forces were there, the police station was there, or anyway that's how things stood, and it's quite beyond any reason that a town would be attacked by Serbian forces if Serbian forces were n control of the town in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you are to avoid the comment, as you well know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to Kosovo and Metohija, General, I think you know -- or, rather, I'm asking you, do you know that there were seven white books, so-called white books, published by the government of Yugoslavia on the KLA crimes committed in Kosovo and Metohija, the NATO crimes in Kosovo and Metohija that were committed, and all the events set out in chronological order which took place and were linked with terrorist activities and NATO attacks on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia? Are you aware of those books?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of those books and I am also aware of everything that was done in connection with them, from the idea to print them and the actual printing and publishing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you take part in reviewing the documents for the book? Did it pass through your hands, those documents and documentation?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope, Mr. Robinson, that you now have sufficient reason to introduce into evidence the white books that I have tendered a number of times. They have been in your possession for quite some time now. You marked them for identification earlier on. The general personally prepared a series of information and facts gathered by the police and ultimately published in those white books, so I hope there are sufficient grounds for the white books to be admitted into evidence, and I should like to tender them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: As we indicated earlier, Mr. Milosevic, we'll consider questions of admissibility of exhibits at the end of the witness's testimony. Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I would prefer to leave it until the end of the evidence, simply to review what the overall evidence on the white books is. Maybe I shan't object. I nevertheless gently observe that the characterisation by the accused of the answer given by this witness doesn't seem entirely to match the witness, unless I've missed something, simply saying he's aware of everything that was -- that the books --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speaker is kindly requested to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I will speak into the microphone and I do apologise. I think at the moment the witness has said no more than it passed through his hands. Where everything that was done and -- yes. It's not the way the accused characterised it, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He says that he's aware of the books and aware of everything that was done in connection with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: A sweeping observation for four volumes of books. Normally, one would have a rather more detailed account of methodology and so on, but in any event, if I could have it until the end of the evidence generally, I'll have a position by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to these books, they are different from the exhibits that we've got before us. They're documents that the Court knows about very well. If the foundation was laid in a little bit more deeper terms with the witness so we could find out the extent of his knowledge. Perhaps it is an issue the Trial Chamber could get out of the way at this stage so that matters that could be raised on them as an exhibit could be dealt with properly by the accused with this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One would have -- one would have expected, Mr. Kay, that the documents would at least be here for the witness to say, yes, these are what I'm talking about, but maybe it's so notorious that it's not necessary, but I wonder if this is rather too much of a shortcut way of trying to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think in relation to them they are very, very well known documents, as Your Honour rightly observes, and they have been mentioned so many times during this trial, and particularly the Defence case, that it may be that that shouldn't be a real obstacle if matters could be explored with him to lay the foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May I add one point which concerned us a little bit at the time. The witness spoke of some of his statistics and charts being identical with or coming from the white book. He didn't provide matching references, and I have to say we haven't been able to find them. I'm not suggesting that the material may not be there, but we certainly haven't been able to find them. So before this witness can produce these documents, I would respectfully invite much more detailed methodology, because otherwise we're going to have to deal with the document if it becomes admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice. Mr. Milosevic, you have heard the objections, if they may be so qualified, from the Prosecutor, as well as the comments of the assigned counsel. You should lay a better foundation to produce these documents through this witness, and I believe that he can, but you need to elicit from him further evidence, for example, as to how the information was compiled and generally to show better familiarity with the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought I could save time, but yes, I will ask the witness a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, how did you collect this information and data, and can you tell us what the methodology applied was? Did you personally take part in preparing this information and preparing the material for publication? Could you explain to us the technology and method according to which that was done, the basic points in the white books?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say first of all that I do apologise if I have created some misunderstanding, because I am doing my best to make my answers brief. Otherwise, I could have explained the whole thing to you but I thought my answer would be rather lengthy and I thought I would be asked subsequent questions. But anyway, it was like this: I attended the meeting of ministers at which the minister declared that there was an idea, an initiative coming from the Ministry of the Interior according to which a collection of documents should be compiled in the form of books where all the information objectively collected linked to terrorist activity in Kosovo and Metohija would be produced and all the consequences thereof. To be as brief as possible, let me tell you that at that same meeting, senior staff meeting of ministers, included experts, analysts to think about the methodology and to propose a concrete methodology for that work, for the work in hand. At the next ministers' senior staff meeting, individuals were appointed and nominated, such as Milos Nedeljkovic, the head of the analytics department, I think he was at that time, and I can't remember what his actual assignment was, or duty was, but then there was Milan Novakovic from the crime police department; they were to head the project. And the way in which the information and data were to be collected was the following: I've already said that the staff of the ministry every morning in their daily morning report would send in information about any event that had taken place, the people who had taken part, and the consequences of the event in question. So this collective information, all the incidents and events that took place were the basis and foundation for compiling the white books, and the tables and photographs and the original police documents or court documents were attached to those lists and that material. So apart from the information supplied by the Ministry of the Interior, we also included certain documents from the Ministry of Justice and the army of Yugoslavia. And I think that that is sufficient foundation for the time being. Of course, I can go on and explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All the information that was included, were they taken from original data and information of the competent authorities on the events mentioned in the white book?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The list of events was copied from original documents and the attending photographs and certain specific documents and photographs taken on location were also taken for the specific events and cases individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That means -- or does that mean to all intents and purposes that the ministry systematised what the ministry had at its disposal in its official documents about the events that took place?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when the books were published. And let me add this: The books or the publisher was the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the printing press was, I think, the Sluzbeni List or Sluzbeni Glasnik, I'm not quite certain, but one of the two companies. And the question raised a moment ago by the Prosecutor, let me say this in response: I did indeed mention that one of the tables from the tabs I mentioned is to be found in the first book, and I think that I remember that it was on page 17 of that book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, you have a good memory. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do I need to ask the witness anything else with regard to those books, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it's really a matter for you as to the foundation that you wish to lay, but in my view you may now proceed and we'll consider this matter later.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to another topic now, another area, General. The units of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia during the war and during the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia, did they spend time on the territory of Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina at all?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police units from Serbia did spend time on the territory of the Republika Srpska and Srpska Krajina on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did those units take part in any of the combat operations?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not except quite -- in special circumstances if they came under attack themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When did the police from Serbia become involved in the border belt with Republika Srpska and how long were they engaged for?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The engagement along the border or rather the pidaliste [phoen] with Serbia, along the border with Republika Srpska, that involvement started sometime at the beginning of 1993 and lasted up until 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Fine. Now, can you show us on the map the area in which the police was present in that border belt, which area of the border belt in our country during the material time, the one we're talking about now.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I can see nothing, by the way, on the screen at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And we're not getting any --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the interpretation now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we're now hearing the interpretation. Perhaps the map could be placed -- could be turned around a little so that the Prosecutor can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On my screen neither Video nor Video Evidence turns up with anything at the moment, if that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be better if it could be placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can the video show the map, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there an answer to Judge Kwon's question? If not, then we could put that particular section -- we're now seeing it. Yes. We're now seeing it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, could you first show the border between Serbia and Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The border can be seen here quite clearly between the Republic of Serbia and Republika Srpska from the north to the south, and I am showing it. I'm indicating it very clearly. This is where the border is with the Republic of Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to show the part where you were, their part of the border as well outside the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period I mentioned, the police units from the Republic of Serbia were in the territory of Republika Srpska in the area around Bajina Basta, Skelani, then in part of the municipality of Visegrad, from Prelovo via Dobrun, then in the territory of the municipality of Rudo in Republika Srpska, from the village of Strpce to the actual town of Rudo, and this place which has the shape of San Marino, surrounded by territory of the Republic of Serbia. It's called Sastavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you understand what this is about. There is a very small part there which belongs to the -- to the municipality of Rudo, right, General?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But actually, it is surrounded by the municipality of Priboj from the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Why was the police engaged there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police was engaged there basically because of the incidents that I described yesterday inter alia. In addition to the two incidents related to the abduction of citizens of the Republic of Serbia at the railway station in Strpce and the abduction of citizens of the Republic of Serbia again but from a bus in Mijocs in the municipality of Rudo. So in addition to that, there were armed attacks by the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina against Skelani and Bajina Basta in mid-January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment. When I asked you about the specific incidents you referred to yesterday, I asked the question whether the paramilitaries were Serb paramilitaries. Were these not different incidents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, Your Honour, I gave a clear and accurate answer. Those two incidents that I described yesterday were carried out by members of paramilitary organisations, Serb paramilitary organisations; that is to say the attack on the bus in Mijocs and the abduction of citizens of the Republic of Serbia and the abduction of citizens from the Republic of Serbia from a train in the village of Strpce was carried out by Serb paramilitary formations, and the attack on Bajina Basta in the Republic of Serbia was carried out by armed formations of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This attack on the citizens of the Republic of Serbia, both attacks that you referred to --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- both were carried out by paramilitary formations in the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Not in the territory of the Republic of Serbia. Just explain so that it would be perfectly clear here how come our citizens were in the territory of Republika Srpska. I bear in mind the fact that the first incident took place on a train and the second one on a bus. How come our citizens were in the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall explain, but may I say that the first one was the bus and the second one was the train, chronologically speaking. The citizens of the Republic of Serbia who at that point in time happened to be in the territory of Republika Srpska were practically forced to travel that way every day because of the configuration of the railway between the municipality of Rudo and the municipality of Priboj in the Republic of Serbia. In order to get to the main town in their municipality, they have to travel through the different municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. You mentioned the municipality of Rudo in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And citizens of the municipality of Serbia, the municipality of Priboj in the Republic of Serbia. When you say citizens, you are saying citizens of Serbia from Priboj, from part of the municipality of Priboj they travelled to the centre of their municipality, Priboj?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So both are in Serbia but if they travel, that -- in that direction they have to cross the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show on the map where this is.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the territory of the municipality of Priboj, if it can be seen properly, and you can see the town of Priboj here. Most of the local communities in the municipality of Priboj are in this sector. In order for these people, the residents of these villages, to get to the main town in their municipality, they have to go through this place called Sastavci surrounded by the territory of Priboj. Then they have to enter the territory of the municipality of Rudo and only then near the village of Uvac, right here, they re-enter the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. As you say, they have to. They have to, that means because they -- the road goes that way?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And there are no other roads?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no alternative roads. Of course as far as the train is concerned the situation is similar, because the train from Belgrade to Bar -- or, rather, that railway goes to Republika Srpska for about nine kilometres and then returns to Serbia in the municipality of Priboj again. So the railway station of Strpce where these persons were abducted also took place on the territory of the Republika Srpska but the persons were abducted from a Yugoslav train on a railway going from Belgrade, Valjevo, Priboj, Podgorica, Bar.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please be asked to speak slower. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is a request from the interpreters for you to speak more slowly. Can you explain to me - I don't know whether you have - who comprised these paramilitary forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I don't know about that. I don't even know specifically who they belonged to, but from all the information that we had, obviously it's a case of paramilitaries because it is said that they were in uniform and with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, can we clarify this. When you say the territory of the municipality of Priboj, Rudo, and around Visegrad, throughout the conflict there were no Muslim forces there; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That is territory that was fully under the control of the Serb forces. So it is absolutely impossible for Muslim paramilitaries to have done this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. The paramilitary forces that carried this out, were they under any kind of control of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the information that we have indicated that they were not under the control of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, for the sake of those who don't know about this, this railway that you were talking about, is that one of the major railroads in the country? It's called Belgrade-Bar, it links Belgrade with the Port of Bar, which is Yugoslavia's biggest port in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Strategically it is indeed one of the major railroads linking to the two republics and also Belgrade to the Port of Bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And that railway, for only nine kilometres, goes through a tiny part of a territory that does not belong to the Republic of Serbia. It is the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this railway station Strpce is outside the Republic of Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was not scheduled to stop there, that train?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some trains do stop there, others do not. It's a small railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did our police do when these citizens were abducted?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When these citizens were abducted, the police, first of all, had more of its own police on these trains, and they took measures through the appropriate authorities of Republika Srpska to investigate the matter as quickly as possible. I personally stayed in Priboj and Prijepolje and that's where the citizens of Sjeverin were from, those who were abducted and also citizens from Prijepolje, those who were abducted from the train. I was there so we could investigate the problem or, rather, shed more light on it in a way, and try to find these people and have them returned to their homes. Regrettably, we did not succeed in doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, so the consequence of that abduction was that a unit of our police constantly controlled that part of the railway that goes through Republika Srpska, that they were protecting people on that train.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only reason for the police forces to cross into this sector of the municipality of Priboj, that is Sjeverin-Sastavci-Strpce was because these two incidents had occurred with grave consequences, and apart from that, there was yet another incident; Kukurevici. That is also a place in the territory of the Republic of Serbia. A paramilitary formation attacked the village, killed a few civilians, and caused considerable damage. That place or, rather, that village is between the Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Montenegro. I'm showing it on the map. It's over here, roughly. Those three incidents were both a reason and a pretext for the police forces to cross the border, to take appropriate positions, and to prevent in the future any kind of similar incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What do you know about the investigations carried out about the abduction of citizens from Sjeverin?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Republic of Serbia, a long-lasting and extensive investigation took place in concert with Republika Srpska. I know that now either in Serbia or in Montenegro there are proceedings under way against some of the suspects involved in that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All these citizens who were abducted, were they all citizens of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all citizens of the Republic of Serbia. Possibly there was an exception. I think there was an ethnic Croat there, but I'm not sure what his actual citizenship was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But they were all abducted in the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all abducted in the territory of Republika Srpska in both cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The presence of our police in that area, did it serve any other purpose except protecting our own rolling stock and the citizens of Serbia in that territory?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our engagement was only aimed at protecting the rolling stock and the citizens of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain the attack on Bajina Basta in the Republic of Serbia now. When did it take place; who carried it out?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The armed forces of the Muslim Federation attacked Skelani in Republika Srpska, which is right across the Drina River from Bajina Basta. I think that this attack happened on the 16th or perhaps the 15th of January, 1993. In that attack, there were between 80 or 90 casualties, persons killed and wounded, and about 1.500 inhabitants fled to the territory of Serbia. A few mortar shells fell on the town of Bajina Basta itself. The gravest consequences were on the bridge itself linking Skelani from Republika Srpska and Bajina Basta in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's just clarify this. Now, towards the end of your sentence you mentioned that the town of Bajina Basta is in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the -- in the Republic of Serbia and Skelani in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But that's on the other side of the Drina River and the Drina is very wide there. Tell me, were shells falling on Bajina Basta?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So was the territory of the Republic of Serbia attacked?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did our police do there in order to prevent further targeting? Bajina Basta is a town, the centre of a municipality.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The centre of a municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of having our forces cross the bridge to the other side of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that sector, our forces crossed the border, I think towards the end of March or the beginning of April 1993. This lasted for about ten days. The objective was to search the area and to practically eliminate the danger that was imminent in terms of the town, the road, going down the Drina River, and in this way to create normal conditions for the functioning of the town and the entire border area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I think that this will do. But I have the impression that you did not explain more specifically and in greater detail the armed incursion of -- from Republika Srpska to Kukurevici, a municipality of Priboj.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the fourth incident I referred to, the third one that the Serb forces took part in. It was in March or April 1993. This is what happened: A group that no one had seen, none of the survivors had seen, crossed over from the territory of Republika Srpska. They crossed the border, they attacked this village in the municipality of Priboj in Serbia. I already said that they torched a few houses, damaged a few houses, and killed five or six, perhaps up to ten civilians, I'm not quite sure now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I think you've explained this very clearly, the road situation, the situation for communicating, and there were no -- there was no possibility of communicating between the same municipality and Serbia except passing through those areas.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, and the only way in which we could protect people from Republika Srpska and vehicles, transport vehicles and so on, was to cross the border and to ensure control over those areas. From the time we crossed the border, there was not a single similar event that took place after that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: People from Serbia, not Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know of our police taking into custody people belonging to paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially in 1992. And I'm quite sure that in 1993 as well there were a number of people who were arrested by the SUP in Uzice. They were suspects and thought to be members of paramilitary groups, and they had crossed over into the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, bearing in mind everything we have stated about the work of the police and how they endeavoured to protect the citizens from paramilitaries during the time of the conflict, could you please give us your comments on what it says in paragraph 24 of what Mr. Nice here calls the Bosnian indictment, where it says that Slobodan Milosevic controlled and influenced the conduct of, among other things, Serbian paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we have been through that approach before where you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Slobodan Milosevic exercised effective control or substantial influence," et cetera, et cetera; paragraph 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I say that we've been through that approach before, which the Chamber does not sanction. You can't ask the witness to comment generally on a paragraph in the indictment. The paragraph may be dissected, it may refer to particular incidents, and you may ask the witness about those particular matters, but not by way of a general comment as to the truthfulness of the allegation in the paragraph, because that ultimately is a matter for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in paragraph (f) of this same section, there is mention of support and direction to Serbian irregular forces or paramilitaries. At that time you were one of the leaders of the police force. Did you have any direct experience yourself about relationships with paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm what I said yesterday and add this: That never personally was I ever in any joint operation with any kind of paramilitary formation nor do I know that anybody from the Ministry of the Interior cooperated in that way or supported any paramilitaries. On the contrary, what I do know is that we always had a negative attitude towards paramilitary units, otherwise we wouldn't have arrested some of their members, as I said in answer to one of the previous questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I omitted to ask you one thing, General, linked to Bajina Basta, as you said that it was an important town and a municipal centre and you couldn't allow bombs to fall in Bajina Basta. But tell me this, near Bajina Basta is there a large hydroelectric power station with a dam?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's upstream about ten to 20 kilometres from Bajina Basta, and it is called the Perucac dam, with a hydro-electric dam there too. Perucac is the name of that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: For us to gain a clear picture of the situation and the involvement of our police force on the other side of the border, you explained that to us in part, but can you just give us the chronology of the steps taken? Roughly speaking, what was the chronology of the events and steps?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with the beginning of the armed conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Serb police first of all strengthened its presence in the border belt towards Republika Srpska. More specifically, they were most numerous in Drina, the Bajina Basta, Ljubovija area, Priboj -- and Priboj, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was upgraded security to protect the state borders? Is that what you mean, upgraded security to protect the state borders?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely it, to protect the state borders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the incident in Bajina Basta, a staff and headquarters was set up headquartered in Bajina Basta and I was at the head of that staff for Bajina Basta. After the withdrawal of the units who had crossed over into the territory of Republika Srpska in the zone of Bajina Basta, and that was sometime in April, the MUP staff from Bajina Basta was relocated to Prijepolje, and sometime in April or May 1993, there was the police involvement on the territory of Visegrad and Rudo across the border in relation to the events I described a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: With respect to the abduction of our citizens.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This involvement and engagement went on until mid-1996, as far as I remember, but certainly up until 1996, perhaps a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean after the war had ended?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, General, I've made a note here of that line which was secured. Is that the line that -- or, rather, could you indicate that line on the map, Prelovo, Dobrun, Strpce, Uvac, Ustival [phoen], Sastavci, Sjeverin, and Cervac [phoen], that axis.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's the line, that's the axis. And I'll show it to you on the map. Prelovo is somewhere in this region, between the Drina River and the border, land border. Dobrun goes up to here. Strpce, as I have already said, would be located here. Ustival is also there; Sastavci are this little circle here; and Sjeverin is between Sastavci and Rudo, somewhere in this region here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, did you have or, rather, were there any activities to take in the Muslim fighters that had sought refuge in Serbia during the time of the attack and the events in Srebrenica? Did you have anything to do with taking them in?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Towards the end of June or, rather, July, mid-July 1995, those units, the units deployed in the region I explained earlier on, took in about 800 fighters of the BH army who, after the Srebrenica operation, tried to cross over into the territory of the Republic of Serbia. And they were put up and accommodated at the centre in Silovica [phoen] near Uzice and were then moved to Mitrovo Polje near Varvarin [phoen] -- or, rather, near Aleksandrovac, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. Now, all these fighters who had crossed over into the territory of Serbia, were they all taken care of and was any violence -- was there any violence against them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. Not even the slightest. They were accepted as people in jeopardy, they were taken care of and accommodated in the collection centre. The Red Cross of Serbia and other humanitarian organisations were informed about their presence, the media and so on and so forth, so everything was public since they crossed over until they left in the direction they wished to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the reasons that you gave us, and if I can just recapitulate and remind us of what you said - and you can tell me if I've left anything out - the unfavourable geographical and topological make-up of the ground for protecting the border and the fact that there were not communicating roads and so on.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the unfavourable position of Bajina Basta itself and the attacks that took place on the territory of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely right; the danger of moving the war to the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in order to secure the state borders. Was there any other purpose to the police's sojourn there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely no. The police presence was there to protect the interests of the Republic of Serbia, to protect its citizens, its settlements, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: With respect to providing safety and security, were the organs of Republika Srpska informed of the measures taken and were they told that we ourselves had to take care of those areas and that we were duty-bound to protect our citizens from the effects of the war?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The organs of Republika Srpska sent in their permission for our involvement on that assignment and we had an exchange of information and coordination of activity with the local organs in the field, in the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain your relationships with the authorities of Republika Srpska with respect to this engagement and when the -- our police were engaged there.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that the Ministry of the Interior was given permission for the -- from the authorities of Republika Srpska. They were not able to take on responsibility for the events themselves, so they gave permission. And then at local level, in the field itself, this idea was put into practice, and after crossing the border there was daily coordination by exchanging information with local police forces in the Visegrad and Rudo municipalities, and of course before that in the Skelani municipality or, rather, the local commune of Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I think that will suffice on that question. Now, let me ask you this: In those assignments and tasks, did the army take part as well, the army of Yugoslavia? When I say "army," I mean army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Yugoslavia took part only in the border crossing in the Skelani zone during those ten days that I mentioned in response to your previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When Bajina Basta was attacked, you mean?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In March and beginning of April 1993, after the attack on Bajina Basta, and never again after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Now, tell us this: How was control and command organised over those police groups and units that were on the other side of the border?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision to deploy the special police units to these assignments across the border was taken by the head of the public sector at the time, and the activities were managed by the staff in Bajina Basta and later on the MUP staff in Priboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you were the head of the Bajina Basta staff?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us this now, please: UNPROFOR, that is to say the UN forces, was UNPROFOR informed of the said engagement and involvement of the police of Serbia on the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to the involvement of the police from the Republic of Serbia, the local authorities informed the international forces and we received feedback information from them that they had done so, that they had informed the international forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, did you know that I informed Owen and Stoltenberg about that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Did the police of Serbia have any other contacts and relations with people in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police of Serbia assisted and provided security for columns of international forces when passing through the territory of Serbia. I personally took part in providing security for DutchBat, the Dutch Battalion, when they withdrew from the territory of Republika Srpska and while they were passing through the territory of the Serbian Republic on to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you took them over, did you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You took them over at the border of Serbia, you took -- escorted them through Serbia, and they continued their journey?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where did you take them over?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took them over in Bratunac and then they entered the territory of Serbia at the bridge in Ljubovija and they went through Lovnica, Sabac and Ruma and entered the Republic of Croatia by the Batovci border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell us this, please, General: During what period of time did our forces -- or, rather, members of our police force, were they present in the Banja Luka area? When were they present there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the broader area around Banja Luka, police units from the Republic of Serbia were present for about 50 days in the period of September 1995. I can't remember the exact period, but I think roughly speaking it was September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was that after the war had ceased in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what was the strength of the MUP forces engaged in the area?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The overall strength of the MUP forces in the area was about 250 to 280 policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In what places in the Banja Luka area were these forces or units deployed, these 250 to 280 policemen? Where were they deployed?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A unit -- units were deployed and carried out their assignments in several municipality towns in Banja Luka; Prijedor, Sanski Most, for example, Bosanski Novi, and Doboj. Perhaps in Derventa and Modrica too but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, explain to us the reason for the engagement of these policemen of ours in that area of Republika Srpska. Why were they there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason for their deployment, for the deployment of the police in Serbia in that area was a request from Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior for reinforcements to help them carry out their daily police duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you received this request for assistance to carry out their regular police duties in the area, did they tell you why they needed this reinforcement?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the request, the reasons they gave was that there was a great influx of people coming in from Srpska Krajina and parts of Republika Srpska itself into that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: During the time those forces were assisting Republika Srpska police as reinforcements, did any armed conflicts break out or clashes between our own policemen and any other armed groups?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were they engaged in regular daily police duties or did they have Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. any other functions?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were engaged to carry out the customary daily routine police duties; patrols, traffic control, crime prevention, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, since you've been a policeman for many years, was that the first time that cooperation in this way was conducted that you know of, the first instance and example?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of several such instances where policemen from Republic of Serbia, for instance, went to other republics of the former Yugoslavia to help out, and I remember one specific case for the Winter Olympics in Sarajevo, the Mediterranean Games in Split, the University Games in Zagreb, and similar large-scale events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this assistance in a time of crisis, was it in a way a similar type of assistance in policework?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very similar but the assignments were somewhat different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about the situation in Republika Srpska with respect to your police duties? How was it reflected on security in Serbia proper, Serbia itself?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything going on in Republika Srpska at that time and linked to the large influx of refugees to the Republic of Serbia of course reflected on the situation in the Republic of Serbia. That is to say the situation in Republika Srpska reflected on Serbia itself because they had to take additional steps to protect refugees who were passing through.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You already said that these forces did not take part in any combat activity.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That pertains to these cases as well?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, on a professional level, subordination, how did these parts of our police function in relation to the police of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As opposed to what happened in Bajina Basta, Visegrad, and Rudo, where we were carrying out our own assignments, as far as this engagement was concerned in the region of Banja Luka, the police of Serbia was carrying out police assignments from the jurisdiction of the police of Republika Srpska, and they were resubordinated to the local police organs in the municipalities where they were operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was that the same pattern as when -- for example, when a gathering in Serbia requires a stronger police presence, a unit of the police from somewhere else comes in and is placed under the control of the local police? Would that be more or less the same thing?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The principle is quite the same because it is logical to have the principle of a single command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you there yourself?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I spent about seven to ten days there, and I visited all the places I've already referred to in order to see for myself how this work was being done and whether there were any problems involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. What about these units of the police that were in the Banja Luka region; what kind of relationship did they have with UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same as I explained for Visegrad and Rudo. The international forces were aware of their presence in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, please, this engagement of the police units in the area of Banja Luka, was that the result of some kind of secret agreement, secret plan, or was this public cooperation and assistance between two police forces?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If was quite public. There was a public request issued by Republika Srpska, and of course it could not have been secret with that many people involved for such a long period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us now how you explained this kind of cooperation after those serious clashes between the authorities of FRY and Serbia and the authorities of Republika Srpska after they rejected the plan of the Contact Group, the Vance-Owen Plan, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Ministry of the Interior, people did not think about that. The objective was quite clear indeed, to help the police of Republika Srpska in a proper way so that they could properly protect large groups and columns of refugees from Croatia and other parts of Republika Srpska. These displaced persons had a very hard time. I saw that for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can it be said that there was no political background involved in this police assistance?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was never my understanding that there was any -- any kind of political background involved in any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in which period were the MUP forces present in Eastern Slavonia and Baranja?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Police forces from the Republic of Serbia stayed in the territory of Baranja and Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misspoke. From mid-August 1995 until, say, January or February 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many MUP forces were engaged in that period in that area?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a rather long period of time, so there were shifts involved, 40-day-shifts, approximately, and the average presence in that territory was between 450 to 500 members of the police force from the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: During the day of these special units, were there any combat actions?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any combat operations otherwise in that area, regardless of whether members of the police of the Republic of Serbia took part?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there was no combat action in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Where were these units of the Serbian police force in Eastern Slavonia and Baranja?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vukovar, Beli Manastir, Ilok, Erdut, Belja [phoen], and a few smaller places. A few.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are all these towns and villages on the very border with the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason for the engagement of the police force there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two reasons. One was the request of the police of the Republic of Srpska Krajina to help them out in carrying out their regular duties, and the second reason was better coverage of the state border between Republika Srpska Krajina and the Republic of Serbia on the Danube.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Why was it necessary to have better coverage and proper coverage of this border?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that from 1992 there was reinforced border control in order -- in terms of Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina in order to control crime, et cetera. So that was one of the reasons, one of the two that I've already explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, what happened in that period of time precisely that required the police of Republika Srpska Krajina to ask for reinforced border control?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time it was assessed that the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia could attack that part of Republika Srpska Krajina. What was expected was a large number of refugees wanting to cross the Danube and all the other problems accompanying that kind of threat. That was the period right after action Storm in the Knin area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was the task of this police force in Slavonia and Baranja?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These units, like in the area of Banja Luka, were doing regular policework; that is to say border crossings, travel checkpoints, traffic checkpoints, patrol. Of course, all in accordance with the plans of the local police commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you there yourself, General?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was there for the most part of this period during the engagement of those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what were the relations like between these engaged units and the police of Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These units from the Republic of Serbia were subordinated to the local police commands. They respected the local authority and the real authority of Republika Srpska Krajina, and I know quite sure -- I know for sure that the international forces were aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any contacts with the Serb Volunteer Guard of Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan in that area?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guard of Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan was in Erdut at the time. A few times I had meetings with some persons from that guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. Were they within the army of Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: According to all the facts that you had available and that are well known, did they have the status of members of the army of Republika Srpska Krajina --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's leading, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As indeed was the previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You must simply ask, "What status did they have?"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, what kind of status did they have?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit of the Serb Volunteer Guard was within the army of Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General -- let me just have a look. To the best of your knowledge, all these engagements of the units of the MUP of Serbia, can they be placed in any way in the context of any kind of aggressive measures against the citizens or the actual territory where they were carrying out the assignments that you described?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no aggressive intentions involved in this engagement of police units outside the Republic of Serbia. I have explained specifically the reasons for it and the objectives for this kind of engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In 20 -- in paragraph 26 of the Croatian indictment, what is mentioned is that members of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia were engaged in some kind of criminal enterprise in SAO -- Eastern Slavonia and Western Srem, SAO Krajina, and the Dubrovnik Republic. Not for me quote all of this. That's what they say; the Dubrovnik Republic. This engagement, does it have anything to do whatsoever with any kind of crime in the territory of the mentioned SAOs; Baranja, Slavonia, Krajina, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This engagement of units that I have just explained has nothing to do whatsoever with any kind of crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking did the MUP forces take part in any kind of combat activities?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we are beyond the time for the break, but I haven't stopped you. I'm getting mixed up. No, we're not. We are taking the first break at a quarter to. By that time you would have concluded your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was my plan, yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In 26(k), Croatia, it says -- there is reference to joint criminal enterprise. I'm not going to quote all of that. "Directed, commanded, controlled, or otherwise provided substantial assistance or support to the police forces within the MUP of the Republic of Serbia..." You are a top official of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. And I quote: "... including the DB, whose members assisted in the execution of the purpose of the joint criminal enterprise of the SAO, SBWS, the SAO Western Slavonia, the SAO Krajina, and the Dubrovnik Republic." General, tell me, please: You said a few moments ago in response to my question that you were present there. You or any other member of the police of Serbia, did you take part in any kind of illegal activity, let alone crime, in that territory?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Every engagement of the police outside the Republic of Serbia is something that I am very familiar with and I know that this engagement has nothing to do whatsoever with any kind of illegal or unlawful activity, let alone any crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, please look at 25, paragraph 25 of the Bosnian indictment. Subparagraph (k): "... formation ... and the special forces took part in carrying out a joint criminal enterprise which is a violation of..." et cetera, et cetera. I don't really have to quote all of it. What kind of special forces are referred to here or any kind of forces that took part in combat activities, in committing crime?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Stop. You said paragraph 25(k) of the Bosnia indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't have (k) in paragraph 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is no (k). It stops at (g).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you speaking of the Bosnia or the Croatian indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I quoted both the Bosnia and Croatian indictment. Both. Both contain such allegations that the police forces -- it always says the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We don't have a 25(k).

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wrote it down. It's on this piece of paper that I have right in front of me. Perhaps I wrote it down wrong but you know full well what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's 25(e).

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So, General, are you aware of each and every engagement of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia outside the borders of the Republic of Serbia, the time, the composition, all the details that have to do with these engagements?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of all engagements of the police of Serbia outside the territory of the Republic of Serbia. My previous answer pertains to this last question of yours too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson. I have completed the examination-in-chief. Now I wanted to ask you whether you think that I should now deal with the additional exhibits or would you like to leave that for later?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we are going to leave the question of the exhibits to the end of the cross-examination, but you made a reference just now to "additional exhibits." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume it's on now. Yesterday, as Mr. Nice explained, invoking Article 68, I received a photocopy. These books, the Phoenix of Freedom, KLA, that's what it's called, and that's where there is a list of all of their dead, and many of the names match the names in the indictment, the names mentioned in the indictment as being those of innocent civilians who were killed in persecutions by forces of the Republic of Serbia, as you call it here. This is what Mr. Nice submitted to me yesterday, so it's not on the list of exhibits. I received it yesterday from Mr. Nice, and I had no way of dealing with it previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Matters of recent disclosure are matters I'll be dealing with in any event under cross-examination, and any that are outstanding can always be tidied up at the end of evidence overall, but I rather doubt if this witness is going to be able to assist. They're not, it seems to me, documents that are likely to assist him but it was judged appropriate to serve the material, or re-serve it, on the accused at this stage given the nature of the evidence he was dealing with. So far as production of exhibits is concerned, I would invite the Chamber simply to put back determination on all matters until the end of evidence, however I must say that there's one matter of procedure touching exhibits that I'm going to ask you to deal with in the absence of the witness. It doesn't actually concern him and is better dealt with in his absence. It will take a couple of minutes, or five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I was going to ask for the time right now, immediately at the break. If -- the witness will get a slightly longer break and he need be confident that what we are going to discuss in his absence has nothing to do with his evidence. It may have something to do with some exhibits but nothing to do with his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us first make a decision about the additional exhibits, and it seems to me that we'll deal with them at the end of the evidence overall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The items you've disclosed sound like things that might persuade a Prosecutor to look at his indictment. That's the impression I'm getting from -- is that a wrong impression?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Rather than the accused have to do something to bring a witness to speak to a book that's been published that perhaps indicates that some of the names in the indictment shouldn't be there as in the categories in which they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour is quite right, it's the sort of material that imposes a further obligation on me, an obligation that I am discharging. But if you will good enough to trust me to deal with it in cross-examination and revert to it at the end of the evidence, I hope that will be the most economic use of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, you may leave now. We are going to deal with a matter in your absence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It doesn't concern you, but you will return after the break. You will be told when to return.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I said you will return after the break, and the court officer will inform you when that will be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Though it's a procedural matter, I would ask that I can deal with it in private session at the moment. It's a private session that will inevitably, as I could judge it, or could inevitably become public later but I ask for private session briefly to explain my position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll start in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, in our submission this is a clear attempt to get round the recent rulings by the Trial Chamber relating to evidence that should be called in rebuttal of the accused's case. It's a way of opening up a window within the Defence proceedings to have a bite of the time that is dressed up as being what we would call a voir dire, a trial within a trial. That's, of course, something that you would have before a jury, and within the jurisprudence of this Tribunal such attempts have frequently been rejected, as reminded recently by the decision in the Delalic case where the Defence had applied for such a procedure to take place and that Trial Chamber rejected it. This Trial Chamber is quite capable of receiving evidence, deciding at the conclusion of the evidential proceedings when it makes its determinations as to what it finds admissible, reliable, unreliable, and it can make decisions at that stage. To have a kind of set-up relating to particularly important Defence evidence is a clever strategy to try and undermine the Defence case as it goes along. One cannot fault Mr. Nice's ingenuity and constant attention to such strategic matters in the pursuit of his goal in relation to winning particular battles within this indictment, but that's really what it comes down to. We have had a rule -- Mr. Nice has referred to material that he gets and how important it is. We've had a Rule 68 disclosure very recently, surprisingly very recently, from a witness called K56: "I never saw anyone being held in the Urosevac SUP, I never heard of anybody being held or mistreated there." Now, if Mr. Milosevic tried to get this in as Rule 68 material, as he's attempted to do at various stages and the Rules have been clarified, it would of course be rejected by the Trial Chamber. It's completely worthless. And when this came into my hands I gave advice that the witness should be called, interviewed, called, called as part of the Defence case. The fact that it comes on a piece of paper with that sort of assertion is completely meaningless and valueless unless that evidence is able to be properly adduced before the Trial Chamber. This is a strategy to get round the recent rules -- the recent rulings. It's why it arises now. It's very close in time to those decisions by the Trial Chamber. And in our submission if the Prosecution themselves have admissible evidence in relation to issues within the defence case, if that evidence is admissible, it should be called as part of their rebuttal case. Otherwise, they should cross-examine on the materials that they have against the witness Jasovic. In linking these documents that are produced by the witness Stevanovic to the Jasovic admission issue, in our submission that is wrong. Exhibits are able to stand on their own and be produced by different witnesses and be admissible under different grounds, and the witness Stevanovic in producing documents that co-relate to those produced or relevant to the witness Jasovic, those documents which arrive here through him as part of the records from the Ministry of Interior and contemporaneous to the time, if they are admissible on that basis, they become admissible in their own right aside of any issues there may be with the witness Jasovic. And Your Honour Judge Bonomy made the point and it's been said it hasn't been made before by us. That's because the ground hasn't been there to make such a submission before. We've not had a witness relating to the archive of materials until this moment, the witness Stevanovic, by whom such materials properly become admissible. And they are plainly relevant to the issue of Article 7(3) responsibility, they're plainly linked to the matters that I raised in open court yesterday concerning the relevance of the procedures and the investigations that were taking place, that the lawful constitutional provisions provided for and that this accused in that dimension is entitled to rely upon in that aspect of his Defence. So in our submission, this application is completely ill-founded. It should be not be entertained as a trial within a trial. There's no good reason for it at all. If they have materials, they should cross-examine Jasovic with those materials and they become admissible and exhibits if they are admissible and exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's your position, Mr. Kay, on whether the accused can rely on these documents for the truth of their contents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's -- for the truth of their contents, it's very difficult. It depends how much is there and whether there's a cumulative background of material that he is able to rely upon.
